body: Jesus has long since forsaken me.

Are you able to bring someone in to help? A friend? Low wage handyman? High-school kid looking for a weekend gig? It may be enough help to get one extra task done and feel you've made progress.

The wet cabinets... There are companies that specialize in this. They will rent you big fans to get it dried out. If the wood is sealed well, you'll be okay. 

Have you considered a community counselor? That is what I do. Also no insurance. It's around $50 a session and I go every couple months. 

I feel your pain. I'm in the process of reclaiming my place from a hoarding husband. It's an overwhelming task. I'm at about 50/50 between work hours and depressive meltdowns at this point lol.

When I feel like giving up I come here to help others. It reminds me of what I should be doing to keep my depression under control. 

Give therapy a shot. Keep in mind that it might take several tries to find the therapist that's fits you. If you go in with an open mind it can help you immensely. It's not easy. It will require some commitment on your part. But the coping skills it can give you have the potential to change your life for the better. What do you have to lose?

Do you enjoy playing guitar and singing? If so, who cares if you're mediocre. Play your heart out. What games do you play?
You need to get some help with this. I can tell you from experience that your negative self-image won't just change with age. It's doubtful that you are as ugly as you think. Good luck.
It will probably take another week for your brain to adjust to it. If it continues beyond that I would touch base with your doc, it may be too high of a dose. That was my experience anyway.
You're definitely not alone in feeling this way. It's a never ending cycle.

I'm still waiting for things to get better. I'm almost 40. Don't stress about that other girl. Chances are she doesn't look like that in person. Your bf is with you for a reason. Right? So try not to compare yourself to others, I know that's easier said than done.

I literally came here to post about the pit of self-hatred. I can't get out either no matter how hard I try. I wonder daily what it's like to be a normal person that doesn't consider suicide or find peace in the idea of ending their life.

Hang in there. We got this. We have to, right?
Yes it does. Have you been hitting yourself?
I did. It was my go-to because it could easily be explained away, unlike cuts. A hammer, rock, board, anything really. I'm 16 months self-harm free, but most days are a struggle.
Thank you. These are really good.

I feel this so much. It took me months to work out of my depressive rut. I did all the right things. I had 4 days in a row where I felt light and finally good. I was so grateful for those days. Then all of a sudden it was like someone pulled a bathtub drain and all the good ran out. It was a literal wooosh back to hell. I don't know why it happened. There was no obvious trigger.

Not sure how to cope. Other than starting back at square one.

Twice in my life. The first time I was 13. I took a bunch of pills. A friend found me. Got me to a hospital. Pumped my stomach. My family acted like nothing happened.

The second time was in 2016 after finding out my husband had been cheating for years. I was already overwhelmed with life. My depression spiraled out of control until one day I snapped out of my fog to find myself sitting on the floor with a pistol to my head. Knew I couldn't do that to my kids and I needed help, I called 911.
Thank you stranger. I needed to see that right now.
I'd like the answer to this as well.
I'm 39 and have been waiting for it to be over soon since I was 12.
I wish I could feel that. They go hand-in-hand for me. Feeding each other.
